source.title: How Does an Agent with Multiple Goals Choose a Target?

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether shared channel responses to different goals reflect polysemanticity, and argues that they instead arise from shared magnitude encoding and spatial gating. It refines the interpretation of polysemanticity, though in a maze-solving RL agent rather than the canonical vision or language examples.
record.gate_note: The study reports results on shared channel responses to four goal entities, spatial gating, and SAE latents. It does not test polysemanticity in image classifiers or language models, or compare architectures, activation functions, or training regimes.
record.test_reason: The study argues that channels responding to four goal entities reflect shared magnitude encoding and spatial gating, not polysemanticity. It does this in a maze-solving RL policy CNN. That is not an image classifier or a transformer language model, and it does not examine canonical polysemantic neurons. The four entities (three keys and a gem) are all goal objects, not unrelated inputs. It reports no share or rate of polysemantic neurons and no comparison of architectures or measurements. Its results therefore do not measure what any version names. The relevant finding is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that the agent reuses shared channels across goal entities, encoding the current target through activation magnitude and spatial gating via negative activations. They explicitly claim SAEs confirm this is not polysemanticity, since latents do not specialise by entity. Patching values beyond the normal range probe weight geometry, while zero-clamping gives the stronger causal evidence.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a trained maze-solving RL agent, parallel rollouts, activation interventions, and SAE-latent patching to investigate goal representation; it is not a direct reproduction of the original polysemantic-neuron examples.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by layer for offset steering: conv2a permits fine-grained steering, while conv1a shows stronger gem steering than later layers. The study also says channel-level details drift across checkpoints.

fits_no_version.finding: Channels in conv3a and conv4a of an RL maze agent respond to all four goal entities, with highly correlated trajectories differing in magnitude. Clamping single channels redirects the agent toward different entities at different values. SAEs with 4x expansion do not split these into entity-specific latents. The authors read this as a shared spatial-gating job rather than polysemanticity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In goal-directed RL CNNs, channels responding to multiple goal entities encode target identity through activation magnitude within a shared function, and SAEs do not decompose them into entity-specific features.

record.problems: Only one environment and a compressed CNN are tested. Most findings are from one checkpoint; some channel-level details drift across checkpoints. Many successful patching interventions require activation values beyond the 99.9th percentile of normal activations. Replication across environments and architectures is left for future work.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant results were left out. Probe accuracies and offset-steering rates were omitted because they measure goal identification or whole-layer steering rather than whether individual neurons have one coherent job or respond to unrelated inputs.

untested.parts: Image-classifier neurons responding to unrelated images.
MLP neurons in transformer language models; prevalence by layer.
Architecture, activation-function or regularization effects on the share of polysemantic neurons.
Canonical polysemantic neurons in vision or language models, re-examined with better tools; how rare truly unrelated mixtures are.
Dependence of polysemanticity judgments on activation range or scoring.

missing.what: conv1a contains highly specialised single-entity detector channels, e.g. five channels above 90% accuracy on blue keys, a contrast to the shared later channels.
SAE reconstruction fidelity: 99.6% (conv4a) and 102% (conv3a) of task performance recovered; 5 SAEs per layer.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V6 link overreaches. V6 concerns canonical polysemantic neurons in vision and language models turning out to detect one shared feature. This study examines an RL policy CNN whose channels respond to related goal entities. It reports no polysemanticity prevalence and does not revisit canonical neurons. Its title-level argument that this is not polysemanticity is in the spirit of V6 but outside its scope, so the finding goes under fits_no_version. Results come from one environment and one checkpoint (channel-level details drift across checkpoints). LessWrong post, not peer-reviewed.

versions.untested_parts: Image-classifier neurons responding to unrelated image inputs; the study uses a maze-solving RL agent and goal entities.
Transformer language-model MLP neurons and unrelated tokens or contexts.
Whether polysemanticity is caused by representing more sparse features than there are neurons.
Polysemanticity arising without capacity pressure from initialization, regularization, or training noise.
The study tests one compressed IMPALA CNN and does not compare architectures, activation functions, or regularization, or report a polysemantic-neuron share or performance tradeoff.
It does not examine canonical polysemantic neurons in vision or language models, nor establish how common shared-feature explanations are across networks.
Whether polysemanticity classifications vary with activation range examined or explanation-scoring method.

rows.baseline: Baseline behavior moves toward the blue key
rows.value: 100% retargeting to regions that are not clamped
rows.locator: Finding 3, paragraph and figure on clamping activations to zero
rows.note: The text says the agent reliably avoids clamped regions even though it can still physically enter them.

rows.measure: Whether an intervention redirected the agent toward an entity
rows.value: Different entities responded to different value ranges within the same channels; successful redirections are shown in the figure
rows.locator: Finding 5, base-model conv4a patching figure and caveat
rows.note: The text explicitly describes the figure as showing multiple entity responses within channels. It cautions that most successful interventions used values well beyond the 99.9th percentile of normal activations.
rows.check: Single channels redirect the agent toward multiple entities at different magnitudes. Most effective values lie beyond the 99.9th percentile of normal activations. The system is an RL policy and the entities are related goal objects, not canonical polysemantic neurons.

rows.subject: SAEs trained on reduced IMPALA CNN conv4a
rows.size_stated: 4x expansion factor; 5 SAEs trained per layer
rows.stage_stated: trained on the trained CNN; SAE training stage otherwise not stated
rows.operation_detail: Applied the same single-location activation-clamping patching approach to individual SAE latents.
rows.measure: Whether individual latents redirected the agent toward entities
rows.value: The same pattern as the base model: individual latents redirected toward multiple entities at different activation magnitudes
rows.locator: Finding 5, conv4a SAE-latent patching figure and accompanying text
rows.note: The authors state that SAE latents did not specialize by entity type. The intervention values are not enumerated in the text.
rows.check: SAE latents show the same multi-entity, magnitude-dependent redirection. This is relevant to the fits_no_version finding, not to V6 as stated.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: The tested maze-solving RL agent, parallel rollouts, and conv4a SAE-latent patching
reader_labels.reason: Channels and SAE latents showed shared, magnitude-dependent responses across goal entities, while natural episode activations and spatial clamping supported a shared spatial-gating interpretation (r1-r8).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Generalization beyond the tested maze-solving RL agent
reader_labels.reason: The study used one environment and a compressed architecture, and does not establish whether canonical vision or language polysemantic neurons generally have shared jobs (r1-r8).
